p: To get the most out of your time slot, arrive a few minutes early so the kids can get their shoes off and socks on without eating into their bouncing time. Comfy clothes without zips or buckles are best, and jewellery is better left at home. A quick chat about taking turns and watching out for smaller children keeps the whole session happier and safer for everyone.

For birthday parties, it's worth asking about party packages and age guidance when you book. If you've got a mix of ages, check whether there are quieter times or areas better suited to toddlers, and keep an eye on the little ones when the big kids are in full flow. Afterwards, a snack and a drink are essential, as tired bouncers turn grumpy quickly.

Salisbury has plenty to balance out all that energy. The cathedral is home to one of the four surviving original copies of Magna Carta from 1215, which is a fascinating thing to show older children. Salisbury Museum, in the Cathedral Close, has displays about Stonehenge and the area's ancient past. The market square comes alive on market days, and the riverside paths along the Avon are lovely for a walk. Further afield, Wilton House and the gardens at Mompesson House are nearby options for a calmer afternoon, giving grown-ups their turn after the kids have had theirs.
